+# dash-codemap
+
+3D, Tron-style map of a git repo (default: `~/Code/personal/dash`). Three.js + Vite.
+
+## Run
+
+```
+cd web
+npm install
+npm run dev                    # http://127.0.0.1:5179
+```
+
+The local scanner (`scan/scan.py`, stdlib only) writes `web/local-maps/<repo>.json`: files with text,
+symbols, imports, per-line blame, working-tree dirty lines, and every commit with its patches.
+Scan any repo with `npm run scan -- <repo path>`; every scanned repo is listed in the menu (Esc)
+and selectable via `?repo=<name>`. The menu also rescans the current one.
+
+## Load any GitHub repo (no backend)
+
+Menu (`Esc`) -> Load from GitHub, or open `?gh=owner/name&n=50`. The browser reads the file tree,
+commit list, and per-commit diffs from the GitHub API and file contents from
+`raw.githubusercontent.com`; nothing is cloned. Unauthenticated limit is 60 API calls/hour; a token
+(kept in `sessionStorage`, sent only to api.github.com) gives 5,000/hour and private repos. History
+is the last N commits, so towers are sized from HEAD and walked backwards through the diffs.
+
+Local scans live in `web/local-maps/` (git-ignored, dev server only). The public build ships only
+`web/public/demo/`; add one with `GITHUB_TOKEN=... npm run demo -- owner/name 60`.
+
+## Sign in with GitHub (optional, Netlify)
+
+The page works without sign-in (public repos, or a pasted token). To add the button:
+
+1. Create a **GitHub App** (preferred: read-only `Contents` + `Metadata`, user picks repos) or a classic
+   OAuth App. Callback URL = the site root, e.g. `https://<site>.netlify.app/`.
+2. Netlify env vars: `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` (server-side), `VITE_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`
+   (public, baked into the bundle), and `VITE_GITHUB_SCOPE=repo` only for a classic OAuth App.
+3. `netlify.toml` already builds `web/` and deploys `web/netlify/functions/github-token.mjs`, which
+   swaps the OAuth `code` for a token and returns only that. The secret never reaches the browser.
+
+Local dev: copy `web/.env.example` to `web/.env.local`; `npm run dev` serves the same function.
+
+## Views and lenses
+
+| View | Geometry |
+|------|----------|
+| City (1) | file = tower (height = lines), folder = district |
+| Graph (2) | import network in free space |
+| Strata (3) | each tower is a stack of slabs, one per commit that touched it |
+
+Lenses (L): change (what the selected commit touched, or the working tree), language, churn, age.
+The timeline scrubs commits; the last stop is the uncommitted working tree. Click a tower for the
+code panel (blame gutter, dirty lines, history diffs, symbols); selected files draw import arcs.

+const TOKEN_URL = 'https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token'
+
+const json = (status, body) =>
+  new Response(JSON.stringify(body), { status, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json', 'cache-control': 'no-store' } })
+
+export default async (req) => {
+  if (req.method !== 'POST') return json(405, { error: 'POST only' })
+
+  const origin = req.headers.get('origin')
+  if (origin && new URL(origin).host !== new URL(req.url).host) return json(403, { error: 'cross-origin request refused' })
+
+  const clientId = process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_ID
+  const clientSecret = process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET
+  if (!clientId || !clientSecret) return json(500, { error: 'GITHUB_CLIENT_ID / GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET are not set' })
+
+  const { code } = await req.json().catch(() => ({}))
+  if (typeof code !== 'string' || !code) return json(400, { error: 'missing code' })
+
+  const res = await fetch(TOKEN_URL, {
+    method: 'POST',
+    headers: { Accept: 'application/json', 'content-type': 'application/json' },
+    body: JSON.stringify({ client_id: clientId, client_secret: clientSecret, code }),
+  })
+  const body = await res.json()
+  if (!res.ok || body.error || !body.access_token) {
+    return json(400, { error: body.error_description ?? body.error ?? `GitHub returned ${res.status}` })
+  }
+  return json(200, { access_token: body.access_token })
+}

+      if (!load) return next()
+      const chunks = []
+      for await (const chunk of req) chunks.push(chunk)
+      const body = chunks.length ? Buffer.concat(chunks) : undefined

+        method: req.method,
+        headers: req.headers,
+        body: req.method === 'GET' || req.method === 'HEAD' ? undefined : body,
+      })
+      const response = await (await load()).default(request)
+      res.statusCode = response.status

+# AGENTS.md: CodeMap
+
+<!-- KEEP THIS FILE IN SYNC: update the map and the hard rules whenever a directory, command or rule changes. -->
+
+CodeMap renders a git repository as a 3D city (Three.js + Vite, no UI framework). A repo becomes a
+**map document** (one JSON file) from one of two producers. The browser app renders whichever it
+gets.
+
+```
+local checkout ─ scan/scan.py ─┐
+                                ├─> map document (JSON) ─> web/src/main.js (Three.js scene + HUD)
+GitHub repo ─ web/src/github.js ┘
+```
+
+## Map
+
+| Path | What | Read next |
+|------|------|-----------|
+| `scan/` | Python scanner for a local checkout (stdlib only) | [`scan/AGENTS.md`](scan/AGENTS.md) |
+| `web/` | The app: Vite config, dev-server endpoints, npm scripts, demo maps | [`web/AGENTS.md`](web/AGENTS.md) |
+| `web/src/` | App source: scene, HUD, GitHub loader, parsers, highlighter | [`web/src/AGENTS.md`](web/src/AGENTS.md) |
+| `web/netlify/functions/` | The one server-side piece: GitHub OAuth code → token exchange | [`web/netlify/functions/AGENTS.md`](web/netlify/functions/AGENTS.md) |
+| `netlify.toml` | Build, publish dir, functions dir, security headers and CSP | this file |
+| `docs/` | README screenshots (taken from public demo maps only) | |
+| `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` | Licenses of the bundled demo maps | |
+
+## Commands
+
+All from `web/`:
+
+```sh
+npm install
+npm run dev                      # http://127.0.0.1:5179, serves local scans + the token function
+npm run build                    # production bundle in web/dist
+npm run scan -- <repo path>      # scan a local checkout into web/local-maps/
+GITHUB_TOKEN=... npm run demo -- owner/name 60   # public repos only, writes web/public/demo/
+```
+
+There is no test suite. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) builds the app and byte-compiles the
+scanner. Check behaviour by running the app.
+
+## Hard rules
+
+- **Private scans never ship.** `web/local-maps/` holds the full source of every scanned repo. It
+  is git-ignored and only the dev server serves it. Never move a scan into `web/public/`, never
+  commit one, and check `web/dist/` before a deploy.
+- **Repo data is untrusted.** Paths, file text and commit messages come from arbitrary GitHub repos
+  and are rendered while a GitHub token may be in `sessionStorage`. Every value that reaches
+  `innerHTML` goes through `esc()` (which escapes quotes, for attributes) or the highlighter's
+  escaping. Never interpolate raw repo text.
+- **The CSP is a contract.** A new network host, inline script, worker or font source needs a
+  matching change to the `Content-Security-Policy` in `netlify.toml`.
+- **Both producers emit the same document.** A field added to the map document is added in
+  `scan/scan.py` and `web/src/github.js` alike (see `web/src/AGENTS.md` for the shape).
+- **Tokens stay in the tab.** The GitHub token goes only to `api.github.com`, is never logged and is
+  never persisted beyond `sessionStorage`.
+- **Demo maps are third-party content.** Only public repos whose license allows redistribution,
+  each with a row in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
+- **No new dependencies without a license check.** Permissive licenses only (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD,
+  ISC). The app has one runtime dependency (three) on purpose.
+
+## Conventions
+
+- Plain ES modules in the browser, no framework. State lives in the `state` object in `main.js`.
+  HUD panels are re-rendered from it with template strings.
+- Python is standard library only, so the scanner runs on any machine with git and Python 3.10+.
+- Comments explain *why*, not what. Commits follow Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, …).

+# Security policy
+
+## Reporting a vulnerability
+
+Please report security issues privately through GitHub:
+**Security → Report a vulnerability** on this repository
+(https://github.com/joellithgow95/codemap/security/advisories/new). Don't open a public issue for
+them.
+
+Include what you found, how to reproduce it, and what an attacker could do with it. I aim to reply
+within a week. This is a personal project, so there is no bug bounty.
+
+## What's in scope
+
+- **The live site** (https://codemap-3d.netlify.app) and the `github-token` Netlify function.
+- **Rendering untrusted repos.** The site renders file paths, file contents and commit text from
+  any GitHub repo while a GitHub token may sit in `sessionStorage`. A repo that can run script
+  in the page, or get the token sent anywhere but `api.github.com`, is a vulnerability.
+- **The local dev server and scanner**, e.g. a way for a web page to read `web/local-maps/` (which
+  holds full source of scanned repos) from a running `npm run dev`.
+
+## How the site protects tokens
+
+- The token lives in the tab's `sessionStorage` only, and is sent only as an `Authorization` header
+  to `api.github.com`.
+- All repo-sourced text is HTML-escaped (including quotes) before it reaches the DOM.
+- The Content-Security-Policy in `netlify.toml` allows scripts only from the site itself and network
+  requests only to the site, `api.github.com` and `raw.githubusercontent.com`.
+- `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` keeps the OAuth `code` out of Referer headers.
+- The OAuth client secret exists only in Netlify environment variables. The function returns the
+  access token and nothing else, and doesn't log it.

+
+<!-- KEEP THIS FILE IN SYNC with scan.py and with the map document shape in web/src/AGENTS.md. -->
+
+`scan.py` turns a local git checkout into a map document at `web/local-maps/<repo>.json` and
+records it in `web/local-maps/manifest.json`. The dev server lists and rescans entries from that
+manifest.
+
+```sh
+python3 -I scan/scan.py <repo> [--out-dir DIR]   # or: cd web && npm run scan -- <repo>
+```

+Relative repo paths resolve against `INIT_CWD` when set (npm sets it to where you ran
+`npm run scan`), else the current directory.

+## What it collects
+
+- Files: `git ls-files` plus untracked, not-ignored files. Text is embedded up to `MAX_TEXT_BYTES`
+  (`MAX_DATA_BYTES` for data formats); binaries and oversized files get `text: null`.
+- Per file: language, line count, Python/JS symbols, Python imports (resolved to repo paths),
+  per-line blame (as commit indexes), working-tree status and dirty lines.
+- Commits: every commit, oldest first, each with its files' add/delete counts and a patch capped at
+  `MAX_PATCH_LINES`. Renames carry `old`, so history follows a file across them.
+
+## Rules
+
+- **Standard library only.** No third-party imports; the scanner has to run anywhere.
+- **Run git with argument lists** (`git(repo, *args)`), never a shell string. Repo paths and file
+  names are untrusted input.
+- **The output is sensitive.** A map holds the repo's full source. Write it only under
+  `web/local-maps/` (git-ignored) unless the caller passes `--out-dir`.
+- **Shape changes go both ways.** A new field is added in `web/src/github.js` too, and documented in
+  `web/src/AGENTS.md`.

+// Builds the "send feedback" link: a prefilled new-issue page on GitHub. Nothing is sent from the
+// app. The link opens in a new tab and the user submits it under their own GitHub account, so
+// there is no token, no API call and no CSP change.

+export const FEEDBACK_REPO = 'joellithgow95/codemap'
+
+const MAX_URL = 7000
+const MAX_NAME = 100
+
+// `context` is { version, view, camera, lens, repo?, userAgent }. Pass `repo` only for a public
+// map (a bundled demo, or a GitHub load made without a token): it lands in a URL that the user may
+// share, so a private repo's name must never get here.
+export function feedbackUrl(context) {
+  const title = 'Feedback: '
+  const head = '### What happened / what I expected\n\n\n\n### Context\n'
+  const fields = [
+    ['App version', context.version],
+    ['View', context.view],
+    ['Camera', context.camera],
+    ['Lens', context.lens],
+    ['Map', context.repo && String(context.repo).slice(0, MAX_NAME)],
+    ['Browser', context.userAgent],
+  ].filter(([, value]) => value)
+  const build = (count) =>
+    `https://github.com/${FEEDBACK_REPO}/issues/new?` +
+    new URLSearchParams({ title, body: head + fields.slice(0, count).map(([k, v]) => `- ${k}: ${v}`).join('\n') + '\n' })
+  // Drop context from the end (the long user agent first) until the URL fits.
+  let count = fields.length
+  let url = build(count)
+  while (url.length > MAX_URL && count > 0) url = build(--count)
+  return url

CodeMap renders a git repository as a 3D city (Three.js + Vite, no UI framework). A repo becomes a

gets.

```
local checkout ─ scan/scan.py ──────┐
GitHub repo ─ web/src/github.js ────┼─> map document (JSON) ─> web/src/main.js (Three.js scene + HUD)
picked folder ─ web/src/local.js ───┘   (reads the folder's .git in the tab via web/src/git.js)
```

|------|------|-----------|
| `scan/` | Python scanner for a local checkout (stdlib only) | [`scan/AGENTS.md`](scan/AGENTS.md) |
| `web/` | The app: Vite config, dev-server endpoints, npm scripts, demo maps | [`web/AGENTS.md`](web/AGENTS.md) |

## Commands

All from `web/`:

```sh

npm run dev                      # http://127.0.0.1:5179, serves local scans + the token function
npm run build                    # production bundle in web/dist
npm run scan -- <repo path>      # scan a local checkout into web/local-maps/
GITHUB_TOKEN=... npm run demo -- owner/name 60   # public repos only, writes web/public/demo/
```

There is no test suite. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) builds the app and byte-compiles the
scanner. Check behaviour by running the app.

## Hard rules

- **Private scans never ship.** `web/local-maps/` holds the full source of every scanned repo. It
  is git-ignored and only the dev server serves it. Never move a scan into `web/public/`, never
  commit one, and check `web/dist/` before a deploy.
- **Repo data is untrusted.** Paths, file text and commit messages come from arbitrary GitHub repos
  and are rendered while a GitHub token may be in `sessionStorage`. Every value that reaches
  `innerHTML` goes through `esc()` (which escapes quotes, for attributes) or the highlighter's
  escaping. Never interpolate raw repo text.
- **The CSP is a contract.** A new network host, inline script, worker or font source needs a
  matching change to the `Content-Security-Policy` in `netlify.toml`.
- **All producers emit the same document.** A field added to the map document is added in
  `scan/scan.py`, `web/src/github.js` and `web/src/local.js` alike (see `web/src/AGENTS.md` for
  the shape).
- **Picked folders stay in the tab.** `local.js` reads files through the browser's folder picker
  and never sends them anywhere; the CSP's `connect-src` backs that up.
- **Feedback never leaks a private repo.** The FEEDBACK button opens a prefilled GitHub issue URL.
  It names the loaded repo only for bundled demos and token-less GitHub loads, never for scans or
  picked folders.
- **Tokens stay in the tab.** The GitHub token goes only to `api.github.com`, is never logged and is
  never persisted beyond `sessionStorage`.
- **Demo maps are third-party content.** Only public repos whose license allows redistribution,
  each with a row in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- **No new dependencies without a license check.** Permissive licenses only (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD,
  ISC). The app has two runtime dependencies on purpose: three, and diff (jsdiff, BSD-3-Clause)
  for the local loader's line diffs.

## Conventions

- Plain ES modules in the browser, no framework. State lives in the `state` object in `main.js`.
  HUD panels are re-rendered from it with template strings.
- Python is standard library only, so the scanner runs on any machine with git and Python 3.10+.
- Comments explain *why*, not what. Commits follow Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, …).

# CodeMap

A 3D, Tron-style map of a git repository. Files are towers, folders are districts, and the commit
history is a timeline you can scrub or play. Load any public GitHub repo in the browser, open a
folder from your own disk, or scan a local checkout.

**Live:** https://codemap-3d.netlify.app · Try a repo: `https://codemap-3d.netlify.app/?gh=owner/name`

![City view of simonw/shot-scraper, coloured by language](docs/city.jpg)

## What it shows

| View | Geometry |
|------|----------|
| City (`1`) | file = tower (height = lines, footprint = share of its folder), folder = district |
| Graph (`2`) | the import network in free space |
| Strata (`3`) | each tower is a stack of slabs, one per commit that touched it |

Lenses (`L`) colour the towers: **change** (what the selected commit touched, or the uncommitted
working tree), **language**, **churn** and **age**. The timeline steps through commits; its last
stop is the working tree. Click a tower for the code panel: source with a blame gutter, dirty
lines, per-commit diffs and symbols. A selected file draws arcs to what it imports and what imports
it.

![Focused on the tests folder: the rest of the city slides away and fades](docs/focus.jpg)

## Getting around

Press `?` in the app for every key and mouse control.

- **Camera presets** (bottom right): TOP (`T`) is an orthographic top-down map where dragging pans
  like a map; ISO (`I`), FRONT and SIDE; FRAME (`.`) fits the selection; ORTHO (`O`) toggles
  orthographic; RESET (`Home`) goes back to the whole repo. The axis gizmo swings the camera to
  look along the axis you click.
- **Folder tree** (top left): the repo at the current commit, each folder with its count of added,
  modified and deleted files. CHANGED hides untouched files.
- **Focus**: click a folder in the tree, click a folder label in the scene, or double-click a tower
  to focus its folder. The rest of the city slides away and fades; `Backspace`, `Esc` (with nothing selected) or the
  breadcrumb goes back up; `Esc` at the top level opens the menu.
- `/` searches files, `←` `→` step commits, `Space` plays the history, `F` free-flies (WASD).

## Run it locally

Needs Node 20.19+ (or 22.12+), Python 3.10+ and git.

```sh
cd web
npm install
npm run dev                     # http://127.0.0.1:5179
```

### Scan a local repo

```sh
npm run scan -- ../path/to/repo   # relative to where you run it
```

The scanner (`scan/scan.py`, standard library only) writes `web/local-maps/<repo>.json` with each
file's text, symbols, imports and per-line blame, the working tree's dirty lines, and every commit
with its patches. Every scanned repo appears in the menu (`Esc`) and at `?repo=<name>`; the menu
can rescan the current one.

> **Local scans contain the full source of the repo.** `web/local-maps/` is git-ignored and only
> the dev server serves it. It never goes into a build. Don't copy a private scan into
> `web/public/`.

### Load from GitHub

Menu → Load from GitHub, or open `?gh=owner/name&n=50`. The browser reads the tree, the last `n`
commits and their diffs from the GitHub API, and file contents from `raw.githubusercontent.com`.
Nothing is cloned and there is no backend in the loop. Without a token GitHub allows 60 API calls
an hour. A token (sign in, or paste one) raises that to 5,000 and reaches private repos.

### Open pull requests

To see how a PR changes the map, use "Browse open PRs" in the same menu section (it lists the typed
repo, or the one on screen), or open `?gh=owner/name&pr=123`. `owner/name#123` and
`github.com/owner/name/pull/123` URLs work in the input too. The city is the tree at the PR's head
and the timeline is the PR's own commits (up to 100), so the CHANGE lens and the commit slider
show exactly what the PR touches. Fork PRs load through the base repo.

Tokens are kept in the tab's `sessionStorage` and sent only to `api.github.com`. The live site's
Content-Security-Policy only lets the page talk to itself, the GitHub API and the raw-content
host.

### Open a local folder

Menu → Open a local folder, or open `?local&n=50`, then CHOOSE FOLDER. This works the same on the
live site and under `npm run dev`, with no scan step: the browser's folder picker hands the files
to the page and everything is read inside the tab. **Nothing is uploaded**, and the CSP would block
the page from sending the files anywhere but GitHub.

History comes from the folder's own `.git`: the last `n` commits on the current branch's
first-parent line (a merge shows everything it brought in), with their diffs, and the working
tree's dirty lines against HEAD. The file list follows the folder's `.gitignore` files and
`.git/info/exclude`, and skips nested repositories as git does. Your global ignore file
(`~/.config/git/ignore`) sits outside the folder, so it isn't applied. Compared with the scanner
there is no blame, renames are found only when the contents are identical, and a worktree or
submodule (where `.git` is a pointer file) opens without history. Chrome, Edge and Arc read the folder lazily. Firefox and Safari read every file in it up
front, `node_modules` included, so use Chrome for big repos.

## Feedback

**FEEDBACK** (under KEYS, and in the menu) opens a prefilled new-issue page on GitHub in a new tab.
It has a "what happened / what I expected" section and a short context block: app version, view,
camera, lens and your browser. The repo name is added only for the bundled demos and for public
repos loaded from GitHub without a token; a local scan or picked folder is never named. Nothing is
sent by the app: you review the text and submit it from your own GitHub account. Without the app,
use **New issue → Feedback** on the repository. If the repository moves, change `FEEDBACK_REPO` in
`web/src/feedback.js` and the link in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`.

## Deploy your own (Netlify)

`netlify.toml` builds `web/`, serves `web/dist`, sets the security headers and deploys one function,
`web/netlify/functions/github-token.mjs`. The page works without sign-in (public repos, or a pasted
token). To add the **Sign in with GitHub** button:

1. Create a **GitHub App** (preferred: read-only *Contents* and *Metadata*, the user picks which
   repos) or a classic OAuth App. Set the callback URL to the site root, e.g.
   `https://<site>.netlify.app/`.
2. Set Netlify environment variables: `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` (server-side
   only), `VITE_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` (public, baked into the bundle at build time), and
   `VITE_GITHUB_SCOPE=repo` only for a classic OAuth App.
3. Deploy. The function swaps the OAuth `code` for a token and returns only the token; the client
   secret never reaches the browser.

For local sign-in, copy `web/.env.example` to `web/.env.local`; `npm run dev` serves the same
function.

To redeploy from GitHub instead of Netlify's own Git integration, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
runs `netlify deploy --build --prod` on every push to `main` and on manual **Run workflow**. Add the
repo secrets `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN` (a Netlify personal access token) and `NETLIFY_SITE_ID`; if
Netlify also builds from Git, turn that off so the two don't race.

The demo maps shipped with the site live in `web/public/demo/`. Add one with
`GITHUB_TOKEN=... npm run demo -- owner/name 60`, for a **public** repo only.

## Project layout

`AGENTS.md` at the root is the map of the code, with a further `AGENTS.md` in each directory for
that layer's rules. In short: `scan/` is the local scanner, `web/src/` is the app (Three.js, no
framework), `web/netlify/functions/` is the OAuth token exchange.

# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please report security issues privately through GitHub:
**Security → Report a vulnerability** on this repository
(https://github.com/joellithgow95/codemap/security/advisories/new). Don't open a public issue for
them.

Include what you found, how to reproduce it, and what an attacker could do with it. I aim to reply
within a week. This is a personal project, so there is no bug bounty.

## What's in scope

- **The live site** (https://codemap-3d.netlify.app) and the `github-token` Netlify function.
- **Rendering untrusted repos.** The site renders file paths, file contents and commit text from
  any GitHub repo while a GitHub token may sit in `sessionStorage`. A repo that can run script
  in the page, or get the token sent anywhere but `api.github.com`, is a vulnerability.
- **The local dev server and scanner**, e.g. a way for a web page to read `web/local-maps/` (which
  holds full source of scanned repos) from a running `npm run dev`.

## How the site protects tokens

- The token lives in the tab's `sessionStorage` only, and is sent only as an `Authorization` header
  to `api.github.com`.
- All repo-sourced text is HTML-escaped (including quotes) before it reaches the DOM.
- The Content-Security-Policy in `netlify.toml` allows scripts only from the site itself and network
  requests only to the site, `api.github.com` and `raw.githubusercontent.com`.
- `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` keeps the OAuth `code` out of Referer headers.
- The OAuth client secret exists only in Netlify environment variables. The function returns the
  access token and nothing else, and doesn't log it.

<!-- KEEP THIS FILE IN SYNC with scan.py and with the map document shape in web/src/AGENTS.md. -->

`scan.py` turns a local git checkout into a map document at `web/local-maps/<repo>.json` and
records it in `web/local-maps/manifest.json`. The dev server lists and rescans entries from that
manifest.

```sh
python3 -I scan/scan.py <repo> [--out-dir DIR]   # or: cd web && npm run scan -- <repo>
```

Relative repo paths resolve against `INIT_CWD` when set (npm sets it to where you ran
`npm run scan`), else the current directory.

## What it collects

- Files: `git ls-files` plus untracked, not-ignored files. Text is embedded up to `MAX_TEXT_BYTES`
  (`MAX_DATA_BYTES` for data formats); binaries and oversized files get `text: null`.
- Per file: language, line count, Python/JS symbols, Python imports (resolved to repo paths),
  per-line blame (as commit indexes), working-tree status and dirty lines.
- Commits: every commit, oldest first, each with its files' add/delete counts and a patch capped at
  `MAX_PATCH_LINES`. Renames carry `old`, so history follows a file across them.

## Rules

- **Standard library only.** No third-party imports; the scanner has to run anywhere.
- **Run git with argument lists** (`git(repo, *args)`), never a shell string. Repo paths and file
  names are untrusted input.
- **The output is sensitive.** A map holds the repo's full source. Write it only under
  `web/local-maps/` (git-ignored) unless the caller passes `--out-dir`.
- **Shape changes go both ways.** A new field is added in `web/src/github.js` too, and documented in
  `web/src/AGENTS.md`.

VITE_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=
# Leave empty for a GitHub App; set to "repo" only for a classic OAuth App that needs private repos
VITE_GITHUB_SCOPE=

# Server-side only (Netlify env vars, or web/.env.local for `npm run dev`). Never VITE_-prefixed.
GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=
GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=

| `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` | Netlify (server) | Same value as `VITE_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` |
| `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | Netlify (server) | **Secret.** Never `VITE_`-prefixed, never in the repo |
| `VITE_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` | Netlify (build) | Public, baked into the bundle |
| `VITE_GITHUB_SCOPE` | Netlify (build) | Empty for a GitHub App; `repo` only for a classic OAuth App |

The `state` parameter (CSRF protection for the redirect) is generated and checked in the browser
(`completeOAuth` / `startOAuth` in `web/src/main.js`). The function only does the exchange.

## Rules

- **Return the token and nothing else.** No logging of tokens, codes or GitHub's response body.
- **Same-origin only.** Requests with a foreign `Origin` get a 403. Keep that check.
- **Fail closed and clean.** Bad input → 4xx JSON. Never throw, and never echo the secret.
- **`cache-control: no-store`** on every response, so no token is ever cached.
- The dev server (`web/vite.config.js`) imports this file directly. Keep it a single default-export
  handler taking a `Request` and returning a `Response`.

## The map document

Produced by `scan/scan.py` (local), `github.js` (`source: 'github'`) and `local.js`
(`source: 'local'`). All three must stay compatible.

```
{ repo, head, branch, generated, [source, owner, truncated, treeTruncated, pull],
  commits: [ { sha, short, author, date, subject,
               files: [ { path, old, add, del, status, patch, truncated } ] } ],   // oldest first
  files:   [ { path, lang, loc, bytes, text, symbols, imports, commits, added, deleted,
               authors, tracked, status, dirtyLines, blame, [sha, binary, remote] } ] }
```

`text` is `null` when not embedded (binary, oversized, or not fetched yet). GitHub loads fetch it
lazily on open. `blame[i]` is a commit index (empty for both browser loaders). `status` is the
working-tree state (`clean` for GitHub loads; `clean`, `modified` or `untracked` for local ones).

## main.js layout

Top to bottom: load (OAuth completion, `?local` folder picker / `?gh=` (+ `&pr=`) / `?repo=` / manifests) → model and layouts → scene
objects (towers, nodes, strata slabs, district outlines and labels) → `applyState()` (recolour and
resize for the current commit, lens and focus) → camera (presets, `fitView`, ortho/perspective
swap, map-mode controls) → focus (`computeFocus` pushes sibling folders apart as rigid blocks) →
HUD renderers (`renderTree`, panel views, legend) → menu, keys overlay and search → keyboard →
`frame()`.

## Rules

- **Borders that pan are fat lines.** District outlines use `LineSegments2`/`LineMaterial` (shader-antialiased, width in px), not `LineBasicMaterial`: a GL line is 1px and unsmoothed on many GPUs even with MSAA, so it crawls while panning. Keep their opacity low (`OUTLINE_GAIN`) or the bloom pass floods the city.

- **Feedback is a link, never a request.** FEEDBACK opens `feedback.js`'s URL in a new tab
  (`<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">`), so there is no token, API call or CSP change.
  Don't turn it into a form (`form-action 'none'`) or a `fetch`. The map's repo name goes into the
  URL only for a bundled demo or a GitHub load made without a token (`source.publicName` in
  `main.js`); scans, picked folders and anything unsure leave it out.

- **Escape everything from a repo.** Paths, names, commit subjects, authors and dates go through
  `esc()` before `innerHTML`. `esc()` covers quotes, so it is safe in quoted attributes too.
  Don't write a new sink that skips it.
- **Network goes through `github.js`.** Only `https://api.github.com` (with the token) and
  `https://raw.githubusercontent.com` (without it). A new host needs a CSP change in `netlify.toml`.
  `local.js` and `git.js` make no requests at all; keep it that way.
- **State drives rendering.** Change `state`, then call the renderer (`applyState`, `renderTree`,
  `renderPanel`). Don't patch DOM fragments ad hoc.
- **Animate, don't jump.** Positions and heights ease toward targets in `frame()` (`vis` = current,
  `focus` / `target` = goal). Camera moves go through `flyTo` / `flyToFit`.
- **Both cameras.** Anything that reads the camera uses the `camera` binding (perspective or
  orthographic). Projection changes go through `applyViewShift()` so the code-panel offset holds.
